newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament lowers personal income taxes.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament lowers personal income taxes.

text.p: Poland's parliament voted on Thursday to change pesonal income tax levels for the next year to 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent from the current 21, 33, 45 percent.
The new tax levels were introduced as an amendment to the government's package of bills, which will be subject to another vote later on Thursday.

Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko earlier said that cutting the lowest tax level to 17 percent was economically unrealistic and would cost next year's budget more than four billion zlotys in lost revenues.

He said during a tax debate in parliament that introducing the 17-percent level would either require a radical cut in spending next year or a substantial increase in the deficit, which would boost inflation.
Deputies voted 220 to 177 with 13 absytentions in favour of the amendment.

On Wednesday, Kolodko asked the lower house, dominated by the ruling left-wing coalition of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and a peasant party, to approve personal taxes at 20, 31 and 43 percent.
He said however, that such tax cuts would require keeping the budget deficit at this year's level of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, rather that cutting it to 2.6 percent as earlier planned.
The tax debate divided the coalition, with the Polish Peasant Party demanding a tax cut for those with lowest income to 17 percent and the SLD supporting Kolodko's proposal.

Central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the 2.8-percent deficit itself might jeopardise Kolodko's goal to slash year-on-year inflation to 13 percent in December 1997 from September's 19.5 percent.
New tax levels may hamper work on the 1997 budget, whose draft the gavernment was due to submit to parliament next week.
